questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Velocity
questions.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t+2t$ meters per second.
Find an expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t+2t) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡t+2) \\  & =2{sec}^{2}⁡t+4.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.problem:
A body of mass $\sqrt{2}\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$  At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡t$ meters per second. 

Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ seconds. Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the force equals
{{field-1}} $\text{N}.$
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sec}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =ma(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F(\frac{\pi }{4})|=|2|=2\,\text{N}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Displacement
questions.problem:
A body of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}$ meters.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=5$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4t-{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4-(-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4+{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=5\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =4+{e}^{5-5} \\  & =4+1 \\  & =5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =4\cdot (5) \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F|=|20|=20\,\text{N}.
$$

The magnitude of the force equals
{{field-1}} $\text{N}.$

According to Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

 
where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t}) \\  & =2\cdot 2{e}^{2t} \\  & =4{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}) & =4{e}^{2\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}} \\  & =4{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}]} \\  & =4{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =4\cdot 2 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}) & =ma(\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F(2)|=|2|=2\,\text{N}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
By Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =ma(t) \\  & =1\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A body of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=t-4\sqrt{t}$ meters.
Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-4\sqrt{t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-4{t}^{1/2}) \\  & =1-4\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot {t}^{-1/2} \\  & =1-2{t}^{-1/2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2{t}^{-1/2}) \\  & =0-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\cdot {t}^{-3/2} \\  & ={t}^{-3/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{t\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =5\cdot (\frac{1}{t\sqrt{t}}) \\  & =\frac{5}{t\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Moments When a Force Has Zero Magnitude
questions.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-6t-36\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-6t-36 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-t-6 & =0 \\ (t-3)(t+2) & =0 \\ t & =-2,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=3\,\text{s}.$

canonical_examples.problem:
A body of mass $2 \, \textrm{kg}$ moves in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\geq 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =2t^3-12t^2-30t+5$ meters per second.
Calculate the time when the force acting on the body has a magnitude of zero.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}-30t+5) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-24t-30\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-24t-30 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-4t-5 & =0 \\ (t+1)(t-5) & =0 \\ t & =-1,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t \geq 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$
